tasks.short: Plan children's and outreach programs, book rooms and partners, take sign-ups, and conduct the programs and library tours.

steps.what: Library technician plans children's programs and community outreach programs
Library technician books rooms and partners by e-mail and phone
Library technician takes sign-ups for programs by phone and at the desk
Library technician conducts the programs and library tours

tasks.design: Rooms are booked in the shared room calendar ({CALENDAR}) instead of by e-mail, and partners get a calendar invitation. Each program has an event page in the library system ({OTHER}) where parents and groups sign up online and get a reminder, so the technician does not take sign-ups by phone. Planning and conducting programs stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rooms were booked by e-mail and sign-ups taken by phone and on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Library systems hold event pages with online sign-up and reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Partners outside the library do not share the room calendar.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a room of six-year-olds listening to a story.

evidence.claim: Library systems can hold event pages with online sign-up and reminders.
Dutch rules set 16 as the age below which a parent consents to a child's data use online.

assumptions: Boundary: from the program idea to the program held; program funding is outside.
Input contract: event pages set up; fallback is phone sign-ups.
Parents sign up online in about the time a call took; a little parent time is priced.
Planning and conducting programs do not change.

incremental.description: Library technician sets up event pages.
Parents and groups sign up online.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small programs with few sign-ups; high: popular programs with many sign-ups.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check in new periodical issues, shelve periodicals and move old issues, review reference materials for outdated editions, and withdraw removed items from the catalogue.

steps.what: Library technician checks in new periodical issues on paper cards
Library technician organizes periodicals on the shelves and moves old issues to storage
Library technician reviews reference materials for outdated editions
Library technician withdraws removed items from the catalogue one by one

tasks.design: The serials module in the library system ({OTHER}) predicts each expected issue, so the technician checks in a new issue with one scan instead of writing on a paper card. Removed reference items are withdrawn in a batch by scanning their barcodes. Shelving periodicals and choosing which reference works to remove stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Issues were checked off on paper cards and withdrawals done one record at a time.
tasks.enabler_now: Serials modules predict issues; library systems withdraw items in batches.
tasks.still_hard: Irregular titles do not follow a predictable pattern.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which old edition patrons still ask for.

reach.learn: Whether new issues reach the shelf sooner.

evidence.claim: Library serials modules can predict expected issues and check them in by scan.

assumptions: Boundary: from issues arrived to the catalogue updated; subscription choices are outside.
Input contract: issue patterns set per title; fallback is checking in by hand.
Shelving and weeding choices do not change.
research_questions: Is check-in time per issue shorter?

incremental.description: Library technician sets issue patterns for new titles.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many irregular titles; high: mostly regular weekly and monthly titles.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Spot missing periodical issues, look up the subscription, write the claim, review the claims, send them to the subscription agent, and record replies.

steps.what: Library technician spots missing issues of periodicals by checking the check-in records
Library technician looks up the supplier and subscription details
Library technician writes the claim for each missing issue
Library technician reviews the claims before sending
Library technician e-mails the claims to the subscription agent
Library technician records claims and follows up the agent's replies

tasks.design: The serials module ({OTHER}) compares expected issues with check-ins and lists issues that are late beyond the agent's claim window, with the subscription and agent details attached, so the technician does not search cards and spreadsheets. Claims are generated from that list. Once the technician has reviewed them, they go to the subscription agent from the module, which logs each claim on the subscription. Following up replies stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Gaps were found by reading cards, and claims written and logged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Serials modules flag late issues and generate claims to agents.
tasks.still_hard: Titles bought directly from small publishers have no agent link.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when a late issue is a publisher delay rather than a loss.
tasks.altitude: The technician reviews claims instead of hunting for gaps.

reach.learn: Whether claims arrive within the claim window.

evidence.claim: Library serials modules can flag late issues and generate claims to subscription agents.

assumptions: Boundary: from the check-in records to replies handled; cancelling subscriptions is outside.
Input contract: claim windows set per agent; fallback is e-mail.
The agent handles system claims as it did e-mailed ones.
research_questions: Do more claims arrive within the claim window?

incremental.description: Library technician keeps claim windows per agent current.

approvals.approved_version: The claims as reviewed by the technician in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many titles bought directly; high: mostly titles through one agent.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Skim the book or reference material, compose the explanatory summary, check it, and enter it in the catalogue record.

steps.what: Library technician skims the book or reference material
Library technician composes explanatory summaries of contents

loop.input: The publisher's description, the table of contents and, where the licence allows, the e-book text.
loop.output: A short draft summary in the library's style.
loop.check: A validator flags any name, title or number in the draft that does not appear in the inputs; the technician edits every draft.
loop.stop: One draft per title; if the inputs are too thin or the draft is rejected, the technician writes the summary.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each book's contents differ; a template cannot summarise them.

steps.what: Library technician checks the final summary
Library technician types the summary into the public catalogue record

tasks.design: A bounded drafting step in the cataloguing tool ({OTHER}) writes a short summary from the publisher's description, the table of contents and, where the licence allows, the e-book text; a validator flags names, titles and numbers not in those inputs. The technician skims the book, edits the draft and checks the final version, which then goes into the public catalogue record. Judging what a reader needs to know stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each summary was written from scratch and typed into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft summaries; cataloguing tools offer drafts the cataloguer accepts or corrects.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts from thin publisher text can be vague or wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Writing for the reader who will pick up the book.
tasks.altitude: The technician edits drafts instead of writing from scratch.

evidence.claim: Alma AI Metadata Assistant drafts a catalogue record from title, author or a title-page photo; the cataloguer accepts, corrects or discards it.
Article 50 sets transparency duties for AI-generated text; here a person edits and takes responsibility for each summary.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new title to the summary published; cataloguing fields other than the summary are outside.
Input contract: publisher descriptions available; fallback is writing from the book.
The technician edits and checks every summary.
Publisher licences allow processing e-book text; otherwise only descriptions and contents are used.
research_questions: How much of each draft does the technician change?

incremental.description: Library technician reports poor drafts to the system manager.

approvals.approved_version: The summary as checked by the technician in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: titles with thin publisher text; high: titles with good descriptions and e-book text.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The library technician keeps running programs, shelving, choosing what to weed and judging summaries; paper check-in cards, phone sign-ups, hand-written claims and summaries from scratch shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time for programs.
